newsitem.title: CHINA: China says understands Russia opposition to NATO.
newsitem.headline: China says understands Russia opposition to NATO.

text.p: China said on Tuesday it understood Russia's opposition to NATO's plans to expand eastwards, but stopped short of throwing its weight behind Moscow.

"We can understand Russia expressing its concern over the issue," Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a news briefing when asked to comment on Defence Minister Igor Rodionov's reported threat to point Russia's missiles at eastern Europe.
Rodionov said in a newspaper interview published last week that one option for responding to NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation) expansion would be to point Russia's missiles at eastern Europe.
Cui took a swipe at NATO.
"NATO is a product left over from the Cold War period. The Cold War has ended. Europe needs a new security mechanism," he told the briefing.
"We hope countries concerned can appropriately resolve the issue through full consultation... the considerations and interests of all countries concerned should be looked after," the spokesman said.

In Lisbon on Monday, Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, spoiling the party at a European security summit, told leaders from more than 50 nations that Moscow rejected NATO's plans to expand eastwards.
Russia says NATO's plans to take in countries of eastern and central Europe, which were Moscow's allies in the now defunct Warsaw Pact, would threaten its security.
But NATO has made clear it will not go back on its plans.
